indicators.name: Atmospheric CO₂ concentration
indicators.notes: March 2026 monthly mean. Threshold specified in methodology v1.0 (450 ppm upper bound). Supersedes the stale Day 1 reading of 424.9 ppm — see CHANGELOG correction, Oct 23, 2026.

indicators.name: Global mean surface temperature anomaly
indicators.source_name: NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4)
indicators.notes: March 2026: +1.30 °C vs 1951–1980 in the source file; converted to the 1850–1900 baseline using the same file's 1880–1900 mean (−0.22) → +1.52 °C. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 2.0 °C, the Paris upper guardrail, consistent with A1's 450 ppm anchor.

indicators.name: Atmospheric methane concentration
indicators.notes: March 2026 global monthly mean. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: deviation 2,400 ppb (≈3,120 ppb total, ~4.3× pre-industrial).

indicators.name: Atmospheric nitrous oxide concentration
indicators.notes: March 2026 global monthly mean. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: deviation 130 ppb (400 ppb total, +48% over pre-industrial).

indicators.name: Radiative forcing — total
indicators.source_name: IPCC AR6 derived — Forster et al., Indicators of Global Climate Change
indicators.notes: Anthropogenic ERF 2.91 W/m² for 2023 (Forster et al.); ~2.8–3.0 for 2024–25. No March 2026 value exists; forcing is a slow integral, so the 2024–25 estimate is the honest input. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 3.5 W/m² (≈ forcing consistent with ~2 °C equilibrium warming at AR6 best-estimate sensitivity).

indicators.name: Stratospheric ozone column
indicators.notes: Global annual mean ≈297 DU per WMO/Copernicus reporting for 2024 (recent years ~296–300 DU). An exact March 2026 global mean is not published in CAMS products. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: deviation 100 DU (one-third global column loss). Ozone is in managed recovery under the Montreal Protocol.

indicators.name: Global mean sea surface temperature anomaly
indicators.source_name: NOAA OISST v2.1 (value estimated from Copernicus/ERA5 reporting)
indicators.notes: Copernicus/ERA5 put 2024 global SST ≈ +1.1 °C over pre-industrial; 2025 cooled slightly from the 2023–24 El Niño peak yet remained 3rd-warmest on record (Pan et al. 2026). A March-2026-specific OISST anomaly vs pre-industrial is not published in that form. Range 0.95–1.15. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 2.0 °C (Paris-consistent anchor, as A2).

indicators.name: Ocean heat content 0–700m
indicators.source_name: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI)
indicators.baseline: 0 (anomaly vs 1955–2006 climatology — proxy baseline; no pre-industrial OHC observations exist. Substitution disclosed in v1.1 addendum §8.)
indicators.notes: Upper-2000 m OHC gained ~23 ZJ in 2025 alone, a 9th consecutive record (Pan et al. 2026); the 0–700 m layer holds roughly two-thirds of that signal. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 400 ZJ.

indicators.name: Ocean pH (acidity index)
indicators.notes: Global mean surface pH from SOCAT/GLODAP-based syntheses; ≈0.12 units below pre-industrial (a ~30–35% increase in hydrogen-ion concentration). A March 2026 global value is not published. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: deviation 0.30 pH units.

indicators.name: Global mean sea level anomaly
indicators.notes: Estimated range 200–240 mm: altimetry contributes ~107 mm since 1993 at a rate now ~4.5 mm/yr; tide-gauge era adds ~100–120 mm before that. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 500 mm.

indicators.name: Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation strength
indicators.notes: RAPID 2004–2023 mean ≈ 16.9 Sv; interannual range ~14–19 Sv; no robust trend detectable in the direct record. Direct observation used per the methodology's named source (model reconstructions run weaker). Baseline 19 Sv = mid of the methodology's 18–20 range. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: weakening of 10 Sv.

indicators.name: Coral reef bleaching extent
indicators.notes: 84% of world reef area exposed to bleaching-level heat stress in the 4th global bleaching event (Jan 2023 – Sep 2025). The event was still officially open as of March 2026; its end was declared June 2026. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 99 points (→100% of reef area).

indicators.name: Arctic sea ice extent — March maximum
indicators.notes: 2026 annual maximum on March 15, 2026; lowest maximum in the 48-yr satellite record (tied with 2025); 1.36M km² below the 1981–2010 average of 15.65M km². Supersedes the 14.22M km² figure repeated in the March 20, 2026 CHANGELOG entry — see correction, Oct 23, 2026. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: loss of 3.0M km² from baseline (stock threshold; see the framing discussion in the reconstruction draft and addendum §4).

indicators.name: Arctic sea ice extent — September minimum
indicators.notes: NEW in v1.1 (addendum §4). 2025 annual minimum, reached September 10, 2025 — tenth lowest in the satellite record (tied with 2008 and 2010). Added alongside C1 rather than re-anchoring C1, per the reconstruction draft's recommendation #1: the March maximum is the slowest-moving cryosphere metric, and a September indicator restores the melt-season signal to the system.

indicators.name: Antarctic sea ice extent
indicators.notes: Annual minimum Feb 26, 2026 — 260,000 km² below the 1981–2010 average minimum (2.84M km²) but 16th-lowest of 48 years (partial rebound after 4 extreme years). Baseline 2.90M km² is an ESTIMATED pre-satellite minimum (the methodology gives no number) — substitution disclosed in addendum §8. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 2.90M km² (complete loss of the summer minimum).

indicators.name: Greenland ice sheet mass balance
indicators.notes: IMBIE/GRACE recent-decade means ≈ −250 to −270 Gt/yr; a March-2026-specific rate is not published. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: −1,000 Gt/yr (≈2.8 mm/yr sea-level rise from Greenland alone).

indicators.name: Antarctic ice sheet mass balance
indicators.notes: IMBIE ≈ −150 Gt/yr for the 2010s; recent years −100 to −250. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: −1,000 Gt/yr (same sea-level logic as C3).

indicators.name: Global glacier mass balance
indicators.notes: WGMS: 2024 ≈ −450 to −517 mm w.e., among the most negative on record; 2025 reported as another extreme-loss year. The March 2026 WGMS release value was not retrieved in the reconstruction pass. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: −1,500 mm w.e./yr.

indicators.name: Arctic sea ice thickness
indicators.notes: Mean winter thickness ≈ 1.9–2.1 m in recent CryoSat-2/ICESat-2 estimates vs ~3.5 m multi-year-ice era. March-2026-specific value not retrieved. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 3.5 m (total thickness loss).

indicators.name: Global tree cover loss
indicators.source_name: Global Forest Watch / Hansen et al.
indicators.notes: 29.9 Mha lost in 2024 (+5% on 2023, fire-driven record) — the latest year that existed as of March 2026. Baseline 2.5 = mid of the methodology's ~2–3 Mha/yr natural range. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: deviation 30 Mha/yr, sitting just above the worst observed year by design.

indicators.name: Tropical deforestation rate (tropical primary forest loss)
indicators.source_name: Global Forest Watch / Hansen et al.
indicators.notes: 6.7 Mha of tropical primary forest lost in 2024 — record high, nearly double 2023, ~50% fire-driven. (A later GFW release put 2025 at 4.3 Mha; it did not exist as of March 2026 and is not used.) Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 10 Mha/yr.

indicators.name: Active wildfire event count
indicators.baseline: Historical frequency baseline (no numeric baseline published)
indicators.notes: EONET is a live feed with no published March 2026 daily-count archive in retrievable form; any specific count would be invented. Excluded from the system mean per the missing-data protocol. Documented context: 2024 fire-related tree cover loss was ~5× 2023 (GFW); March is a seasonally low-fire month. v1.1 substitution defined in addendum §5.

indicators.name: Global forest carbon stock anomaly
indicators.notes: ESTIMATED, low confidence. FAO FRA 2025 puts today's total forest ecosystem carbon at ~650–660 GtC; pre-industrial stock estimates (~830–860 GtC) come from potential-vegetation modelling (Erb et al. lineage), not the FRA itself — the two are not perfectly commensurable. One of the weakest inputs in the reconstruction. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 400 GtC of stock loss.

indicators.name: Primary forest cover remaining
indicators.notes: Current primary forest ≈ 1.11 Bha (FAO FRA); estimated 1850 primary forest ≈ 5.1 Bha (HYDE land-use history: ~5.9 Bha total forest in 1850, ~85–90% primary). Ascending indicator: under the general function with baseline 100 and threshold 100, the score equals the remaining percentage.

indicators.name: Forest regrowth rate
indicators.baseline: Natural regeneration baseline (no numeric value in methodology — documented alternative ratio form used)
indicators.threshold: Ratio form: score = expansion ÷ concurrent deforestation × 100
indicators.notes: Forest expansion 6.78 Mha/yr (2015–2025, FAO FRA 2025, released Oct 2025); same source: gross deforestation 10.9 Mha/yr, net loss 4.12 Mha/yr. Score = 6.78 / 10.9 × 100 = 62.2 — does regrowth offset loss? Documented alternative form adopted in v1.1 (addendum §2).

indicators.name: Living Planet Index
indicators.notes: Average −73% change in monitored vertebrate populations, 1970–2020 (Living Planet Report 2024, the latest edition existing as of March 2026). BASELINE SUBSTITUTION disclosed in addendum §8: the methodology asks for the index 'normalized to 1850,' which the LPI does not publish; the 1970-anchored value is used. Score = index × 100 (direct form).

indicators.name: Species extinction rate
indicators.source_name: IUCN Red List derived (Pimm et al. 2014 and successors)
indicators.threshold: Log form: S = 100 × (1 − log₁₀(rate ÷ background) / 4); zero at 10⁴ × background
indicators.notes: Current rate ≈ 100 E/MSY, ~1,000× the low background estimate; plausible range 50–200+. The methodology's linear function cannot score a quantity spanning 3 orders of magnitude (it returns ~90 for a mass-extinction-rate signal), so v1.1 adopts the documented log-scale form (addendum §2): extinction risk is multiplicative and each order of magnitude is an equal ecological step. Background 0.5 = mid of the methodology's 0.1–1 range; log₁₀(200) = 2.30 → 42.5.

indicators.name: Global biodiversity intactness index
indicators.source_name: Natural History Museum / PREDICTS (Newbold et al. 2016)
indicators.notes: Global mean BII 84.6% as published (Newbold et al. 2016) — but the value describes ~2005; no newer global BII has been published. Used as the closest documented value and flagged as two decades stale. Direct form: score = BII.

indicators.name: Marine protected area coverage
indicators.baseline: Natural baseline (not meaningful for a protection construct — scored against the Kunming–Montreal 30×30 target instead; see notes)
indicators.notes: Protected Planet reporting for 2024–25: ~8.2–8.4% of the ocean in MPAs. Construct note: a pre-industrial 'baseline' for protection is meaningless (nothing needed protecting), so v1.1 scores coverage against the 30×30 policy target (addendum §2). 8.2 / 30 × 100 = 27.3.

indicators.name: GBIF occurrence record density anomaly
indicators.notes: Not merely missing but ill-defined: GBIF publishes occurrence counts, which grow with digitization and observer effort; no 'density anomaly vs historical species density' product exists, and raw record growth would score a healthier planet the more phones people buy. Excluded. v1.1 replaces this indicator with the Red List Index (addendum §5).

indicators.name: Insect biomass index (proxy)
indicators.source_name: Literature synthesis / Hallmann et al. 2017 framework
indicators.notes: −76% flying-insect biomass over 27 years in German protected areas (Hallmann et al. 2017) — used exactly as the methodology names it ('Hallmann et al. framework'), with the caveat that it is a regional proxy standing in for a global quantity nobody measures. Direct form: score = % remaining.

indicators.name: Global drought index — SPEI
indicators.notes: The SPEI database is gridded; no single published 'global SPEI' value for March 2026 exists, and computing one is a research task, not a retrieval. Excluded rather than estimated. v1.1 substitution — a computed, area-weighted global SPEI mean with published method — is defined in addendum §5.

indicators.name: Global groundwater storage anomaly (scored as depletion rate)
indicators.source_name: GRACE-FO (estimate per Wada et al. lineage)
indicators.notes: ESTIMATED, low confidence: global depletion ~250–330 km³/yr in recent assessments; cumulative depletion since the mid-1900s >10,000 km³. BASELINE SUBSTITUTION disclosed in addendum §8: GRACE-era anomalies are referenced to a 2004–2009 mean, not a pre-industrial state, so the indicator is scored as a depletion rate vs a pre-depletion (≈zero net rate) equilibrium. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 500 km³/yr sustained depletion.

indicators.name: Global freshwater withdrawal as % of renewable supply
indicators.notes: Global water stress 18.6% (FAO SDG 6.4.2, latest published cycle). Baseline PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 5% (low-demand historical level; the methodology specifies only 'historical low-demand baseline'). Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: deviation 45 points (50% global stress = 0).

indicators.name: River flow anomaly — major basins
indicators.notes: Not retrievable as a March 2026 global percentage. Documented context: WMO's State of Global Water Resources reports 2024 as the sixth consecutive year in which a majority of the world's basins ran below normal — qualitative categories, not a global anomaly figure. Excluded. v1.1 substitution defined in addendum §5.

indicators.name: Lake water level anomaly
indicators.unit: % of large lakes in significant decline
indicators.source_name: HydroSat / Copernicus (proxy: Yao et al. 2023, Science)
indicators.notes: ESTIMATED proxy: Yao et al. 2023 found 53% of the world's large lakes lost significant water volume, 1992–2020. This storage-decline share stands in for the methodology's level-anomaly share; the named HydroSat product does not publish a single global March 2026 figure. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 100%.

indicators.name: Transboundary water stress index
indicators.notes: The Pacific Institute's Water Conflict Chronology is an event database, not an index with a baseline; no numeric value of this indicator has ever been published. (Nearest documented relative — SDG 6.5.2 transboundary cooperation coverage, 59% in 2023 — measures a different construct and was NOT substituted into the baseline.) Excluded. v1.1 substitution = SDG 6.5.2, defined in addendum §5.

indicators.name: Global soil organic carbon stock
indicators.source_name: FAO GSOC map / ISRIC (Sanderman et al. 2017, PNAS)
indicators.notes: 133 GtC lost from the top 2 m since the advent of agriculture (Sanderman et al. 2017 — the standard estimate underlying FAO soil-carbon-debt reporting). Value expressed as loss vs the pre-agricultural stock (baseline 0 = no loss). Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 400 GtC loss.

indicators.name: Land degradation index
indicators.notes: 'Up to 40% of the planet's land is degraded' (UNCCD GLO2, 2022) — also the figure in the Day 1 notes. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 100% (deliberately the plain linear reading; the sensitivity analysis tests a sterner 50% threshold).

indicators.name: Desertification proxy — NDVI anomaly in arid zones
indicators.baseline: Stable vegetation index (no numeric baseline published)
indicators.notes: No single published global index value for March 2026 exists. Documented context cuts the other way: the global NDVI trend is net greening (CO₂ fertilization + land management), with arid-zone results regionally mixed — so excluding S3 likely biases this system DOWNWARD, and that direction of bias is disclosed here. Excluded. v1.1 substitution defined in addendum §5.

indicators.name: Soil erosion rate
indicators.source_name: FAO / Borrelli et al. global erosion model
indicators.notes: 35.9 Gt/yr water-driven soil erosion (Borrelli et al. 2020 update of the global RUSLE model — the FAO-cited standard). Natural/geologic background ≈ 12 Gt/yr (ESTIMATED). Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: deviation 48 Gt/yr (total ≈ 60 Gt/yr, ~5× background).

indicators.name: Topsoil depth loss rate
indicators.notes: No global statistic of this form exists in published GSP/FAO products; soil monitoring networks are national and non-harmonized. Excluded. v1.1 substitution defined in addendum §5.

indicators.name: Nitrogen deposition anomaly
indicators.notes: ESTIMATED, low-moderate confidence: global mean deposition over land ≈ 7 kg N/ha/yr (total reactive-N deposition ~90–100 TgN/yr over ice-free land) vs the methodology's pre-industrial 1–2 (1.5 used) — an anomaly of +5.5 kg N/ha/yr. Hotspot regions exceed 30–50. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: deviation 20 kg N/ha/yr (a global mean at today's hotspot levels).

indicators.name: CDP disclosure quality — portfolio weighted average
indicators.source_name: CDP public disclosure grades (via CONSCIENCE dataset, data/conscience-data.json)
indicators.notes: Portfolio CDP grades {A×1, A−×6, B×16, C×9, D×4} mapped on the methodology's stated anchors (A=100, D=0) with linear interpolation (A−=83.3, B=66.7, C=33.3) — the mapping grid is a v1.1-adopted PROPOSAL; the grades are data. Direct form: score = mapped mean.

indicators.name: SBTi 1.5°C approval rate — % of portfolio companies
indicators.notes: 9 of 36 companies hold validated 1.5 °C targets (a 10th holds an approved operational target). Direct form: score = approval rate.

indicators.name: Active climate litigation count — portfolio total
indicators.source_name: Sabin Center Climate Litigation Database (via CONSCIENCE dataset)
indicators.notes: Sum of Sabin active cases across the 36-company portfolio = 135, matching the dataset's own metadata total. Threshold PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1: 200 cases.

indicators.name: Corporate lobbying alignment score — portfolio weighted average
indicators.notes: Portfolio InfluenceMap grades {B+×1, B×3, B−×5, C×8, C−×8, D×7, D−×2, F×2} mapped F=0 → A+=100 in equal letter steps (mapping grid PROPOSAL adopted in v1.1; grades are data). Cross-check: the CONSCIENCE methodology's own lobbying factor mean, 32.2 normalized, lands close. Direct form.

indicators.name: SEC 8-K material disclosure event density
indicators.notes: Not retrievable from any local record: the dataset's EDGAR block stores only CIK URLs; the v2.8 platform computed 8-K density live but no March 2026 value was ever recorded. Rebuilding it would require a fresh EDGAR pull for a past window — doable in Phase 2, not honestly fillable here. Excluded. v1.1 makes CA5 a computed-at-scoring-time indicator (addendum §5).

indicators.name: Science-based emissions trajectory alignment — portfolio % on 1.5°C path
indicators.source_name: VYRION CONSCIENCE derived / SBTi (v1.1 differentiation via TPI — see addendum §6)
indicators.notes: REDUNDANCY DISCLOSED: in the current dataset CA6 and CA2 are the same measurement (both = the 9 SBTi-approved companies). The baseline retains the value as computed; v1.1 differentiates CA6 using the TPI levels already carried per-company in the CONSCIENCE dataset (addendum §6), effective from the next scoring cycle. Direct form.

history.note: Restated baseline — reconstructed from published inputs (methodology v1.1)
